In reference to the
question:	-
Has a report been received by the government from Sir Henry Thornton . . . What is the exact terms of the recommendation in question?
The information was laid on the Table at the request of the hon. member on May 1. As to the question:
What action has been taken or will be taken by the government ?
I answer: Under consideration. In regard to the fourth query:
Will a copy of the reply of the government be laid on the Table of the House, and when?
A copy of the reply to the Minister of Railways is laid on the Table now:
May 14th, 1924.
Dear Sir Henry Thornton:
I understand the contents of the letter written me by you on April 9th re the Toronto viaduct have been given out in Toronto. I find I cannot lay my hand on copy of any reply sent you but there certainly should have been an acknowledgment, at least. On the day after the receipt of your letter, if I mistake not, a large deputation from the city of Toronto waited on the government and expressed their views from every angle. The Prime Minister reviewed at length the conditions. Since that date, however, conditions have been somewhat changed possibly by the fact that it has come to my notice the Harbour Commission has entered action against the railways and the city of Toronto.
At the present moment I am awaiting a full statement of the case, legally and otherwise, from the Canadian National Railways. When that is received, consideration will be given by the government as to the next step to be taken.
Yours sincerely,
Geo. P. Graham.
Sir Henry Thornton, K.B.E., President,
Canadian National Railways,
Montreal, Que.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
speechtext:
I think I should draw the attention of the House to the character of this question. The first clause reads:
Have any representations been made to His Majesty's government of Great Britain regarding the British preference and the damage done to Canada from its withdrawal or part of it as per the recent British budget?
The last clause is:
What damage has< been done to Canadian industries in the new budget re the British preference, and what communications, if any, have been received or named by the government on the question?
These two questions contradict each other.
I do not think that as at present drafted the question is in proper form to present to the House:	It would involve a reflection by one
government upon another within the British Empire. I think it should be withdrawn.

And the opinion of one
government might not be the opinion of another.

The question might be
re-drafted and presented in more acceptable form.
Dropped.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: I regret to be obliged again to object to the production of these papers. The order calls for information which is of a confidential character and which it would be subversive of public interest to disclose. Apart from these general reports, monthly reports are received from the officer commanding the police describing the work done in connection with the enforcement of the Narcotic Drug Act. Even these are of a confidential nature. But I am quite willing to let my hon. friend use such files as he thinks contain information which he would like to have. I must, however, oppose the motion for the production of these papers.
All I ask is for the production of such records as it is proper to produce.

Carried as amended.
PRIVILEGE-MR. GARLAND (Bow River)
On the Orders of the Day:

Mr. Speaker, I rise to a question of privilege. I was absent yesterday when the House met, having to keep an important appointment. However, my attention has been called to some remarks by the hon. member for Belle-chasse (Mr. Fournier), who read from the Ottawa Journal the following words:
Mr. Fournier, of Bellechasse, absent from House (though in Ottawa) without a pair.
Then he said:
Thursday morning I had an urgent call to go out of town. I made arrangements to leave Friday morning at 6.55, and I kept my engagement. Had it not been for some of my hon. friends, particularly the hon. member for Bow River (Mr. Garland), I would have had ample time to vote and my vote would have been recorded as in favour of the budget.
I must respectfully decline, Mr. Speaker, to allow the hon. member to use my name under these circumstances as an excuse for his not being present and voting. It was through no desire of my own that I was compelled to speak at that late hour, but I exercised my undoubted privilege in so doing. May I suggest that had the hon. member arranged a pair all this trouble would have been avoided?

Civil Service Superannuation

Hon. .1. A. ROBB (Acting Minister of Finance) moved that the House go again into committee on the following proposed resolution :
Resolved, that it is expedient to bring in a measure to provide for the superannuation of civil servants, to provide for contributions by civil servants to the consolidated revenue fund, to provide for payment out of the consolidated revenue fund to civil servants and to the widows and children of deceased civil servants of superannuation allowances or gratuities, and to provide for the making of regulations by the Governor in Council to give effect to the terms of the said measure.
Explain.

The bill to be introduced will be based upon the recommendations of a special committee that had this matter under consideration at the last session of parliament. Hon. members will recall that that committee reported to the House on the 22nd of June last year, too late for consideration of the report at that session. On that occasion the Prime Minister promised that consideration would be given to the matter this session. We had hoped to bring down the bill a little earlier, but owing to the debate on the budget it has been delayed. It is now proposed that after the bill is introduced it shall be referred, with the concurrence of the House, to a special committee, possibly the same committee that considered the matter at the last session.
When the bill was first printed it was intended that it should come into force on the 1st of July this year, but as it has been somewhat delayed the committee may in their judgment change the date. That will be a matter for further consideration. I submit that the whole matter might very well be left to the committee.
